races.title: State Senate, District 44
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ted Alexander
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina Senate District 44 since January 2019. Former Mayor of Shelby (elected 2003, re-elected 2007). Worked as a Main Street downtown revitalization director in Virginia and Shelby. Has a Cornell master's in historic preservation. Lost the 2014 U.S. Senate Republican primary to Thom Tillis.
cands.gaps: The pages we could read did not show how Alexander has voted or what bills he has sponsored in the state Senate, so we have no legislative deeds to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. His only recorded position on abortion is a 2014 campaign statement. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020 through 2026. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements. His birthplace and upbringing come only from his own campaign site, with no independent confirmation.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born and raised in Morganton, NC, attended local schools and UNC-Charlotte, and later served as Mayor of Shelby (2003-2011) and as a state senator since 2019.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2019 (7 years; Ballotpedia lists chair posts on several committees). Mayor of Shelby 2003-2011. Executive director of Main Street downtown revitalization programs in Bedford, VA and Shelby, NC, and Virginia State Main Street Director 1994-1996. New York State Senate Fellow. Master's in historic preservation.
qual.why: He has seven years of prior legislative service and two terms as mayor, plus a career in economic development and public policy work. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has seven years of prior legislative service and two terms as mayor, plus a career in economic development and public policy work. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: On his 2014 U.S. Senate campaign website he described himself as "pro-marriage, pro-family, and pro-life." This is a 2014 statement, not a legislative deed.

cands.name: Rod Powell
cands.bio: Retired public school teacher with a 30-year career in North Carolina classrooms, including Lincoln high school in Vale and Mooresville city schools. Lives in Casar, Cleveland County, and chairs the Cleveland County Democratic Party. Democratic nominee for NC Senate District 44 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended in the voter guide "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Sway voting group by Vote for Peace).
Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended in the voter guide "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions from Powell on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. He has never held elected office, so there is no legislative record. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. His exact birth date and the years he taught at each school were not found. No news coverage of him was available.

local.label: Roots 80: His campaign biography says he was born in Anderson, SC, his family moved to Greensboro, NC in 1978, he graduated from high school there in 1980, and he then attended UNC-Chapel Hill and taught in NC schools for 30 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He taught in North Carolina public schools for 30 years, holds National Board Certification and a master's in education, and chairs the Cleveland County Democratic Party. No legislative or local elected office, and no policy or budget career, appears in the sources.
qual.why: A long teaching career is real-world work, but it is not a legislative, policy or budget role. No prior elected office is documented. A party chair post is not an elected office.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He says he will support competitive teacher pay and better teacher retention. He also says he will keep public education funding focused on schools that serve all children, and he does not address vouchers or charters directly.
